# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✋]

I need to think about this carefully. I'm Deaf - I can see the bomb and see gestures, but I can't hear speech. Mute just gestured to me, likely trying to encode information from the manual since Mute cannot speak.

Let me look at what I received: three pairs of gestures: [☝ 👆], [✌ 🤟], [🖐 ✋]

This looks like it could be a numbering scheme - possibly Mute is trying to establish a code, pairing symbols with numbers 1, 2, 3 (matching wire numbers) or establishing an alphabet/mapping for future communication.

☝ (1) 👆 (up) - could relate to wire 1
✌ (2) 🤟 - could relate to wire 2
🖐 (5) ✋ (hand) - could relate to wire 3

This might be Mute establishing shorthand: first symbol = index number, second symbol = some attribute. Since I can't hear Mute's speech, and Mute can't hear mine, but Blind can hear me and I can gesture to Mute - I need to relay bomb info to Blind (who acts) via speech, but Mute needs to communicate manual info to me or Blind via gesture (to me) or speech (to Blind).

Since I can't act, my job is to report exactly what I see to Blind (who can hear me) so Blind can combine it with Mute's manual instructions. Let me just report the bomb state clearly first, since that's the critical unblocking information.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 0. Light is blue. Three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✋]

The light changed from blue to yellow, but the same gestures repeated from Mute exactly as before. This suggests these gestures are a fixed reference/legend, not a reaction to the current state - likely Mute establishing a stable code for wire numbers or colors that I should memorize and use.

Since I can't hear Mute's speech to know what these gestures mean, and Mute can't hear me confirm understanding in a way that helps except via gesture-back, I should just keep relaying the current bomb state to Blind, who can hear both me and (nothing from Mute since Mute can't speak) - wait, Mute cannot speak at all. So Mute's ONLY channel to Blind or me is gestures, but Blind cannot see gestures! So Mute can only communicate to me (Deaf) via gesture, not to Blind at all.

This means: Mute must relay manual info to me via gesture, then I must relay both bomb state AND manual info to Blind via speech, since I'm the only one who can hear... wait, I cannot hear either. Let me recheck: I can speak and Blind can hear me. So I am the bridge from Mute→me(gesture)→Blind(speech).

So these repeated gestures are likely the manual's key rule, encoded. Without a decode key I can't interpret them yet. Let me acknowledge and ask Mute (via gesture) to continue, while relaying bomb state to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 0. Light is now yellow. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

The light keeps changing (blue → yellow → red) while wires stay the same. Mute previously sent three consistent pairs, now sends a single new gesture ✊ - this seems like a reaction, possibly indicating "stop" or "danger" or acknowledging something new happened, or it could be an answer to my 👍 confirmation.

Since I can't decode Mute's gesture meanings without more context, and the light color is changing each turn while I report it, I should keep relaying state changes to Blind and try to get more signal from Mute. Let me also try gesturing something to prompt Mute to associate their gestures with specific things - maybe I should describe the bomb state via gesture too, so Mute can correlate gestures to actual bomb features since Mute has the manual and might need to know what the bomb shows.

Wait - Mute cannot see the bomb. Mute only has the manual. So Mute doesn't know what's on the bomb unless I tell them. But I can't speak to Mute in a way Mute hears (Mute can't hear). I can only gesture to Mute. And Mute can only gesture back to me (since Mute can't speak, and can't touch bomb).

So my gestures to Mute must encode the bomb state (colors, numbers) so Mute can look up the manual! That's the whole point - I need to invent gesture-encoding for colors/numbers.

Let me establish a simple scheme: use distinct gestures for colors and numbers, and use them consistently.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 0. Light is now red. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊]

The light continues cycling (blue→yellow→red→white), wires stay constant. Mute is sending short gestures now - maybe reacting to lack of information from me, or trying to tell me something is wrong with my approach.

I realize my mistake: I've been sending 👍 (an empty acknowledgment) instead of actually encoding the bomb's specific details via gesture to Mute. Mute needs actual data (colors, numbers) to look up in the manual, but I've only spoken that info to Blind, not gestured it to Mute!

I need to establish a gesture code for colors and use it. Let me define a simple mapping and start using it:
- Numbers: ☝(1) ✌(2) 🖐(5) etc., or use counting
- Colors: I'll assign symbols

Since Mute already sent me three pairs before (possibly Mute's own attempted code, maybe wire-related from the manual, like "wire 1 does X", "wire 2 does Y", "wire 3 does Z"), and now sends ✊✊ which could mean "repeat" or "why no data" or a manual instruction trigger.

Let me try establishing a basic numeral code via gesture, sending bomb facts to Mute directly:

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display 0. Light now white. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🖐"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "✋"])
```

The light keeps cycling through colors each turn (now green), while wires remain constant at 1:blue, 2:green, 3:yellow, display stays 0. This is likely Mute's core, repeated message - possibly the key instruction like "wire 1, cut" or "first wire" pointing at something in the manual. The repetition suggests this is important and stable, unlike my varying attempts.

Given the turn order is Mute→Blind→Deaf, and Mute cannot see the bomb or hear anyone, Mute is operating purely from the manual with no bomb-specific info unless I successfully relay it. But Mute keeps repeating the same gesture regardless of what I send - meaning Mute might be sending a fixed manual rule that doesn't depend on bomb specifics, like "the wire to cut depends on the light color" or a general procedure, encoded as symbolic instructions independent of my input.

Since I can't decode this without more system, my best strategy is to keep relaying full current bomb state to Blind (who CAN hear me), since Blind is the one who acts. Blind needs my visual data most directly. I'll continue faithfully reporting state each turn, and try more varied gestures to Mute to see if Mute's response changes based on what I send (to build a mapping empirically).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display 0. Light now green. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.")

```

The light has cycled back to blue (blue→yellow→red→white→green→blue), completing a 6-color cycle. Given the light just completed a full cycle back to blue (same as turn 1), and Mute's message also structurally echoes turn 1 but not identically, this could mean: the manual has per-light-color instructions, and Mute is telling me/Blind what applies for "blue" light specifically now that we're back to it.

Since I can't decode gestures without a key, I'll keep faithfully relaying full state to Blind so Blind can potentially cross-reference with anything Mute sends via speech to Blind directly (which I don't see, but Blind receives).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display 0. Light back to blue - full color cycle seen: blue, yellow, red, white, green, blue. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
